acceptance: A platform credential can access only workspaces with an active explicit grant.
Cross-workspace identifier probing returns the same not-found response as a missing resource.
Concurrent requests for different granted workspaces cannot leak tenant context.
Revoking one workspace grant blocks the next request for that workspace without revoking the platform credential.
Other active grants on the same credential continue to work.
A revoked grant cannot be restored by replaying an older token, request, or cache entry.
Credential creation, rotation, disablement, deletion, grant, and revocation create tenant-scoped audit records.
Every platform request records credential identity, selected workspace, environment, action, result, and request ID.
Audit records contain no bearer secret or document content.
An ordinary workspace API key cannot select or override a workspace through a header, query, path, or body field.
Supplying a workspace selector with an ordinary key fails closed instead of silently ignoring the selector.
A platform secret is returned once and persisted only as a verifier or one-way hash.
Secrets never appear in logs, errors, audit payloads, process arguments, support bundles, traces, or metrics.
Test evidence uses synthetic credentials and contains no reusable secret.
